definition: Falsifiable means able to be proven wrong by evidence or observation.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word falsifiable. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know falsifiable should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Her claim that the cat opens the pantry at night is falsifiable: one cheap camera on the shelf settles it either way.
An arguable claim can be batted back and forth with reasons forever, and no round of debate ever finishes it; a falsifiable claim is braver — it points to evidence that could end the matter for good.
A testable claim lets some evidence bear on it; falsifiable is the strictest rung — it names the exact result that would prove the claim dead wrong.

Disprovable is falsifiable's plain-English twin: evidence could show the claim is wrong. Falsifiable is the laboratory's version of the same virtue and adds the emphasis scientists prize — the claim itself spells out, in advance, exactly which observation would kill it.

Refutable belongs to the debate hall: a refutable claim can be knocked down with arguments, counterexamples, and logic. Falsifiable moves the contest outdoors — it is settled by observation rather than rhetoric, and the falsifiable claim names the measurement or find that would prove it wrong.

Falsifiable means able to be proven wrong by evidence or observation.
The bridge foreman's boast — 'this deck will not flex more than a centimeter under a fully loaded train' — is falsifiable in the most literal way.
Mount a gauge, run the train, read the needle: past one centimeter, the boast dies on the spot.
Compare the mayor's speech that the bridge is 'a triumph of civic spirit,' which no needle anywhere can touch.
Falsifiable is praise in science's own tongue: a claim brave enough to name what would prove it wrong.
The centimeter boast stakes itself on a needle; the 'triumph' line risks nothing and so, to a scientist, says nothing.
The word doesn't mean false — it means honest enough to be testable to destruction.
Falsifiable is a term of praise in laboratories: a claim honest enough to name its own kill switch.
Keep it near its unit-mates — a falsifiable claim can be tested, a replicable result survives the retest, and a tenable theory is still standing afterward.

Duarte returned every science-fair proposal with one question scrawled at the top: what result would prove you wrong?
Half the class was baffled.
Surely the point of a hypothesis was to be right.
She explained that a claim earns its place in science by being falsifiable — by naming, before the experiment starts, the exact observation that would kill it.
Lena rewrote her proposal to say that if the shaded beans grew as tall as the sunlit ones within three weeks, her light hypothesis was finished.
It survived, as it happened.
Duarte gave the ribbon less for the result than for the risk the claim had agreed to run.
